# FDG5003

> AVOID being inconsistent in the ordering of parameters in overloaded members. Parameters with the same name should appear in the same position in all overloads.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.1.1 Member Overloading.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5003
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Put the parameter '{0}' at the same position in every overload of '{1}'

FDG5003 reports a parameter of an externally visible method or constructor whose position differs from that of the parameter with the same name in another overload declared in the same type. `params` arrays and `out` parameters are left out, as the body allows, and so are CancellationToken parameters, which section 9.2.2 keeps last. In constructors of an exception type, a leading `string message` and a trailing `Exception innerException` (or `inner`) are left out before positions are compared, because section 7.4 fixes where the common forms `(string message)` and `(string message, Exception innerException)` put them; the parameters between them are compared. Overrides and interface implementations take their signature from another member and are not reported, and overloads inherited from a base type are not compared. There is no code fix; moving a parameter changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking.

## From the book

```csharp
public class EventLog {
   public EventLog();
   public EventLog(string logName);
   public EventLog(string logName, string machineName);
   public EventLog(string logName, string machineName, string source);
}
```

In some specific cases, this otherwise very strict guideline can be broken. For example, a `params` array parameter has to be the last parameter in a parameter list. If a `params` array parameter appears in an overloaded member, the API designer might need to make a trade-off and either settle for inconsistent parameter ordering or not use the `params` modifier. For more information on the `params` array parameters, see section 5.8.4.

Another case where the guideline might need to be violated is when the parameter list contains `out` parameters. These parameters should typically appear at the end of the parameter list, which again means that the API designer might need to settle for a slightly inconsistent order of parameters in overloads with `out` parameters. See section 5.8 for more information on `out` parameters.
